```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(RdistNN)
```

This guide explains the covariance and status fields returned by
`affine_ratio_dnn()` and `clate_dnn()`. Start with the
[CLATE workflow](conditional-late.html) for inputs and a complete example.
For identification, nuisance-learning conditions and asymptotic inference,
see the accompanying [paper](https://jakobjuergens.com/research/#orthogonal-inference-conditional-z).

## A small paired-signal example

```{r fixture}
fit <- affine_ratio_dnn(
  X = matrix(1:4, ncol = 1), x0 = 0,
  numerator = c(2, 1, 4, 3), denominator = c(1, -1, 2, 1), s = 2
)
fit$components
summary(fit)$coefficients
```

The numerator and denominator use the same weights, and their paired
covariance enters ratio uncertainty. Dividing the numerator SE by the first
stage or discarding the component cross-covariance gives a different
calculation. Deletions hold supplied signals and geometry fixed; nuisance
models are not refitted.

## Keep the variance scales distinct

| Returned field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `components[, "numerator"]` | Reduced form for a CLATE fit |
| `components[, "denominator"]` | First stage for a CLATE fit |
| `component_vcov[[j]]` | Paired component covariance on the estimator scale |
| `theta_vcov[[j]]` | Ratio variance on the estimator scale |
| `theta_omega[[j]]` | `neff[j] * theta_vcov[[j]]`, local-limit covariance estimate |
| `se[j]` | Square root of the ratio variance |
| `neff[j]` | Inverse sum of squared reporting weights |

`theta_vcov` already includes the local sample-size scaling. Do not divide
it by `neff` again. Covariance lists are marginal across reporting targets;
they do not supply covariance between different targets or simultaneous
confidence bands.

```{r reporting}
summary(fit)
confint(fit)
diagnostics(fit)
```

Effective sample size describes rank-weight concentration. It is not a
count of compliers. Physical radius, instrument-arm support, score
dispersion and first-stage strength can vary even when `neff` is the same.
The largest centered pseudo-value-square shares attribute fitted variance
to deletion indices, including rank changes; they differ from raw weighted
score contributions.

## Signed signals and unavailable intervals

Augmented treatment signals can be negative even with one-sided compliance;
they are not individual compliance indicators. A finite negative aggregate
denominator gives a signed ratio, without replacement or trimming.

Inspect these fields before reporting a CLATE result:

| Field | What to check |
|---|---|
| `ratio_status` | `ok`, zero denominator, component overflow or ratio overflow |
| `negative_denominator` | A finite negative first stage |
| `near_zero_denominator` | Numerical cancellation; not a calibrated weak-IV test |
| `covariance_status` | Available, missing, zero-score or numerically failed covariance |
| `wald_available` | Whether the reported SE supports the computational Wald output |

An exactly zero first stage gives an undefined ratio while retaining component
estimates and available covariance. Exact zero score variance gives SE zero
and unavailable Wald bounds. A finite ratio may also have unavailable
uncertainty. These cases stay visible in summaries and plots; inspect the
first stage and status rather than interpreting missing bounds as precision.

CLATE generally differs from an average of stratum-specific LATEs or an
ordinary residualized-IV coefficient. Use the paper's estimand definition
when choosing the appropriate workflow.

## Ratio confidence sets

The experimental `ratio_confidence_set()` helper uses the paired
estimator-scale covariance. It can return bounded intervals, singletons,
half-lines, two rays, all real numbers or empty sets. It remains separate
from `confint()`, which reports pointwise Wald intervals.

```{r confidence-sets}
ratio_confidence_set(fit$components, fit$component_vcov)
sets <- ratio_confidence_set(
  rbind(c(2, 1), c(3, 0), c(0, 0)),
  list(diag(c(.5, 0)), diag(2), matrix(0, 2, 2))
)
sets
vapply(sets, function(x) x$type, character(1))
```

Finite endpoints are included. An `unresolved` result reports a numerical
status without asserting a set geometry; it differs from a mathematically
empty set. Materially indefinite or unavailable covariance is rejected.
See `?ratio_confidence_set` for input validation and returned fields.

Neither a finite Wald interval nor this experimental inversion establishes
uniform coverage under weak first stages. The paper describes the scope of
its inference results. Numerical safeguards and successful array tests do
not establish the statistical assumptions for a particular application.
